subject: Dedicated capacity runbook for low-latency feature rollout - exception request
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity runbook for low-latency feature rollout - exception request

Team —

We have a tight launch window for Atlas Labs (pilot customer) to ship the low-latency chat experience on Dec 8. Product has validated latency SLOs, but achieving them in production requires a short-term carveout in the dedicated GPU pool and a temporary autoscale soft-exemption for their route.

Key asks:
- Reserve a 48-hour reserved buffer daily (08:00–20:00 PST) on a dedicated A100 pool slice for 2 weeks spanning Dec 6–19.
- Temporarily relax the autoscale cap for that slice to allow burst to 1.6x baseline while monitoring queue depth.
- Ops runbook + on-call escalation path for fallback to quantized variant.

I've attached a capacity proposal and a draft ops checklist. Marcus: can you confirm Atlas's expected concurrent streams (they've quoted 300 concurrent active sessions peak) and the internal cost target? Jonas/Laura: can infra and product accept the temporary exception gating and the rollback criteria in the attached draft?

I know this is an exception to our standard reservation SLAs — we need to document the risk and the rollback plan before I confirm with Atlas procurement.

Thanks —
Olga
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity runbook for low-latency feature rollout - exception request

Olga —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. A few clarifying questions from infra:
1) "48-hour reserved buffer daily" — do you mean a reserved band that stays allocated 08:00–20:00 PST, or a rolling 48-hour window overlap? Please confirm exact slot semantics.
2) Which model variants are acceptable as fallbacks? We need a verified, quantized variant with throughput tests.
3) What telemetry/alerts do we want to bake into the runbook (token latency p50/p95, queue depth, KV cache hit rate)?

Operational constraints: changing autoscale caps requires an ops-approved change request and a 24h stub period for monitoring. For a short carveout we can create a temporary pool label (atlas-pilot-ll) and attach special autoscale rules, but we will need signoff from Capacity Stewards (Kimberly) to preempt existing queued reservations if contention occurs.

I'll prototype a slim runbook and load tests Monday. If Marcus can confirm expected RPS and normal session length, we can translate into token/sec and quantify the slot count.

— Jonas
Sr. Infra Engineer

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity runbook for low-latency feature rollout - exception request

Adding product context: Atlas Labs' low-latency feature is a gated pilot for their customer support product. The behavioral profile is chatty: 4–6 short turns per session, median prompt length ~30 tokens, but critical 99th percentile latency needs to be <150ms token emission for UI snappiness.

If we rely on a quantized fallback, quality regressions are acceptable during bursts only if we fail over gracefully with user messaging. The launch KPI is availability under load and perceived responsiveness — not raw sample quality.

I'll work with Jonas on the rollback criteria: propose automatic rollback if p95 latency > 250ms for 10m or if queue depth > 25 for 5m. Also need a preflight run during low-traffic hours.

Laura
Product Manager, Dedicated

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity runbook for low-latency feature rollout - exception request

Olga/joined —

Atlas confirms 300 concurrent active sessions peak, average session duration 4 minutes, expected sustained period of 2 hours during release validation. Pricing target aligns to a 20% uplift over baseline dedicated rate for the pilot; they've accepted a short-term fee. I've attached an updated capacity-cost sheet (capacity-proposal-v2.pdf).

Request for Ops: we need the reserved band 08:00–20:00 PST Dec 6–19 (daily persistent allocation) rather than a rolling 48h, otherwise Atlas can't guarantee test coverage in their markets. For autoscale: allow burst up to 1.6x baseline but gate by token budget and require explicit rollback if cost per token > threshold (I've put a conservative threshold in the sheet).

If Capacity Stewards approve, I'll finalize the PO and procurement will sign the contract with the exception window.

— Marcus
Account Lead, Strategic Apps

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sofia Moreno <sofia.moreno@atlaslabs.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 14:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity runbook for low-latency feature rollout - exception request

Thanks everyone — consolidated plan below and next steps:

Plan (high level)
- Reserved band: create label atlas-pilot-ll and allocate N=4 A100 slots 08:00–20:00 PST daily for Dec 6–19. (Jonas to confirm exact slot translate to token/sec).
- Autoscale exception: cap increased to 1.6x for atlas-pilot-ll, with automatic throttle if cost/token > $0.0025 (Marcus threshold).
- Rollback triggers: p95 token latency >250ms over a 10m window OR queue depth >25 for 5m.
- Fallback: auto-failover to quantized model variant (atlas-quant-v1) with a staged A/B banner on UI.
- Monitoring: add p50/p95 latency, queue depth, KV hit rate, pool utilization to the runbook and onboard PagerDuty alerts to the capacity-oncall.

Action items
- Jonas: produce an ops-checklist with exact commands/playbook and preflight run (due Wed Nov 25 COB).
- Marcus: finalize PO/fees and send procurement terms (due Tue Nov 24 EOD).
- Laura: finalize rollback wording and user messaging for fallback (due Tue Nov 24 EOD).
- Kimberly: please confirm approval to preempt queued reservations if contention occurs.

Sofia (Atlas) — attaching the plan here. If this looks good we'll push the exception request into Capacity Stewards and queue the change ticket.

Olga

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity runbook for low-latency feature rollout - exception request

Approve the temporary carveout under the following constraints:
- Limit preemption to non-enterprise queued reservations; no SLA violations for existing enterprise committed pools.
- Require a daily health digest for the Duration Window (Dec 6–19) with explicit cost burn and latency trends.
- If we see two consecutive days where rollback criteria are triggered more than 3 times, the carveout will be revoked and Atlas billing will be pro-rated.

Jonas: proceed to create the atlas-pilot-ll label and put the change request into the ops queue. I'll backfill approvals in Steward board.

— Kimberly
Head of Capacity Stewardship
